cim: ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet argues against cutting China off, warning that aggressive export controls will drive Beijing to accelerate domestic development (Reed Albergotti/Semafor)
cim_eredeti: ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet argues against cutting China off, warning that aggressive export controls will drive Beijing to accelerate domestic development (Reed Albergotti/Semafor)
szoveg_eredeti:
Export controls on chips and other technology shouldn’t aim to cut China off completely — a strategy that will only backfire, warns Christophe Fouquet, CEO of ASML, the sole maker of the lithography machines needed to produce the world’s most advanced AI chips.

“You need [export controls] to protect very advanced technology, but you also have to use export control in such a way that you don’t completely frustrate a country and invite that country to basically double down or triple down on development,” Fouquet said on Semafor’s Future Proof.

The debate over Chinese access to Western technology has intensified in Washington after revelations of Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy left lawmakers divided on how aggressively to tighten curbs.

As a $520 billion de facto monopoly in chipmaking equipment, ASML sits at the center of that fight. Fouquet argued that continuing to sell China older equipment — ASML’s shipments there are more than a decade behind the cutting edge — maintains a strategic “generation gap” that keeps Beijing hooked on Western hardware rather than racing to build its own.

“For almost 30 years, we have been able to keep an extremely high market share in China — very high means close to 100% — which means that they have accepted to rely on our technology with the idea that they had access to it,” Fouquet said.
